A.explanation: A metre rule reads to about $0.1 \text{ cm}$, so it cannot give the required $0.01 \text{ cm}$ precision.

B.explanation: A micrometer reads to $0.001 \text{ cm}$ but its range is typically only about $2.5 \text{ cm}$, so it cannot measure about $10 \text{ cm}$.

C.explanation: A tape measure reads to about $0.1 \text{ cm}$ and is for larger distances, so it cannot give $0.01 \text{ cm}$ precision.

D.explanation: Vernier calipers read to $0.01 \text{ cm}$ and have a range over $10 \text{ cm}$, so they meet both requirements.

hints: Notice the two demands together: a length of about $10 \text{ cm}$ and a precision of $0.01 \text{ cm}$ or $0.1 \text{ mm}$.
Recall the typical precision and range: metre rule and tape measure to $0.1 \text{ cm}$, vernier calipers to $0.01 \text{ cm}$, micrometer to $0.001 \text{ cm}$.
Check which instrument with $0.01 \text{ cm}$ precision also has jaws that open wide enough to span $10 \text{ cm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the requirements: distance $\approx 10 \text{ cm}$ and smallest readable change $= 0.01 \text{ cm}$.
Recall precisions: metre rule $\approx 0.1 \text{ cm}$, tape measure $\approx 0.1 \text{ cm}$, vernier calipers $\approx 0.01 \text{ cm}$, micrometer $\approx 0.001 \text{ cm}$.
Eliminate metre rule and tape measure because $0.1 \text{ cm}$ is ten times too coarse for $0.01 \text{ cm}$ precision.
Compare range: a micrometer typically measures only up to about $2.5 \text{ cm}$, so it cannot span $10 \text{ cm}$, while vernier calipers typically measure up to $10$-$15 \text{ cm}$.
Therefore vernier calipers satisfy both precision and range. This is option D.
